2 · Paste the post copy

A hearing on Anchorage's police AI rule was set for September 1st, 2026. The camera money passed 8 to 4 that night. The rule got no vote.

$598,998 in federal asset forfeiture money for the Real Time Crime Center.
Three of the four no votes wrote the ordinance.
ADN reports it would require Assembly permission before AI with human feature recognition joins the network.
Anchorage banned municipal facial recognition in 2023, per APD's own page.

The carousel plots the network's real size on a log rule. 11 cameras integrated against 238 registered as of August 27th, 2026, under a 750 ceiling.

Sponsors plan to bring it back on September 15th, 2026. What does a no vote from the rule's own authors buy once the money is already spent?

#AnchorageAssembly #SurveillanceOversight #AlaskaPolicy

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

Editor's note

This is an EXPLICIT UPDATE to Carousel No.40 of August 25th, 2026, which covered the same ordinance before the hearing. The dedupe gate fired a LIKELY DUPLICATE and the update route is the one way through it, so the cover says UPDATE and names what changed. Two corrections the fact-checker forced, both worth knowing. The vote was Tuesday September 1st, not September 3rd. And municipal facial recognition was ALREADY BANNED by the Anchorage Assembly in 2023, which is on APD's own page and is why slide 07 leads with what is already in code. The ordinance text itself was never obtainable, so every provision is attributed to a newsroom on the slide and in the caption.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11am Alaska time.
  • Paste the first comment immediately, inside the first 60 seconds.
  • Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. A dead first hour is rarely recovered.
  • If a commenter asks whether Anchorage runs facial recognition, the answer is no and the Assembly banned municipal use of it in 2023, per APD's own page. Do not soften that.
  • If a commenter asks for the ordinance text, say plainly that it is not publicly reachable and that every provision on the deck is attributed to the newsroom that reported it.
  • The September 15th, 2026 meeting is the live hook. Anyone who asks how to testify can be pointed at the Assembly's own testimony process.
  • Watch for saves and sends rather than likes. Slide 04 is the one built to be saved.
